A prompt can give you a starting point.
It doesn’t magically give you taste, debugging, optimization, and iteration.

originalText:
A 24-year-old in Chengdu made 71,400 yuan (~$9,800) last month from 47 mobile games

He never wrote more than 200 lines of code in his life

Claude Fable 5 wrote the other 800,000

Total Claude spend for 11 weeks: 1,847 yuan

Pause at 3:02. That is not a Mario emulator. That is a working clone of Super Mario 1-1 built in 4 minutes 58 seconds. Pixel-perfect art. Original physics. NES color palette. Custom font. Level data. Full game engine. 1,213 lines of game.js. 149 lines of level.js. All generated in one session

He did not run it as a fan project

He repainted the sprites. Renamed Mario to something the store would approve. Changed the green pipes to red. Shipped it on TapTap as "Mushroom Adventure."

It made 4,200 yuan in the first week

He shipped 6 more variants the same month

By month 2 he had 12 games live. By month 3 he had 47

The games are not masterpieces. He knows that. They do not need to be. They need to be cheap, fun, and finished.
The Chinese App Store does not care which model wrote the code

It cares whether the game runs

He took a screenshot of the final Mario build. He prompted Claude to make it darker, faster, and remove the mushroom

That became game 33

The internet said AI cannot ship products that real users will pay for

47 games. 11 weeks. One developer who has never written a real codebase

The store does not need him to be a developer

It just needs him to keep pressing submit

The whole 11-week run cost him less than dinner for two in Shanghai

Save this. The next 1,000 games on the store you have not opened in a year will not be made by studios

originalText:
Claude Fable 5 went 5 for 5.
Opus 4.8 failed.
And Mythos - Anthropic's most powerful model - never even stepped on the field.

Someone decided to run a real test.
Five tasks you wouldn't expect from AI:
Map every asteroid in the Solar System using live NASA data.
Rebuild Apollo control panels from technical PDF files.
Build a World Cup shirt supply chain based on live game results.
Simulate the effect of solar storms at dawn.
Design a 100-acre fitness retreat layout.
Opus 4.8 — failed on several.
Fable 5 — passed all of them. Without exception.

But here's what most people missed.
Mythos — Anthropic's real flagship — wasn't even in the room.
It's locked inside Project Glasswing.
Available only to a handful of trusted organizations worldwide.
The public has never seen what it can do.

What just beat everything — isn't even their best version.
It's just what they decided to give us.

Makes you wonder what the people with real access are building right now.
